γυῖον.definition: limb, Hom., always pl., in phrases such as Il.13.85; 14.506; 4.230, etc., cf. A.Pers.913 , Id.Eleg.3; the feet, Il.13.512; womb, h.Merc.20; hands, Theoc.22.81; sg., the hand, ib.121 ; but the whole body, Pi.N.7.73, Hp…

γυλλός.definition: block of stone, Schwyzer 725 , SIG57.25 ; also Hsch

γύναιος.definition: = presents made to a woman, Od.11.521.15.247; Mosch.2.45. II. Subst. little woman, term of endearment for a wife, Ar.V.610, Th.792: more freq. in a contemptuous sense, weak woman, And.1.130, etc.; D.25.57, cf. Arist.E…

γύνανδρος.definition: of doubtful sex, womanish; of a woman, virago, Ph.1.183,2.379

γυρῖνος.definition: or tadpole, Pl.Tht.161d, cf. Arat.947; Lib.Decl.26.36

γῦρις.definition: the finest meal, Dsc.2.85, Sor.1.118, Ath.3.115d, POxy.520.12 :—also prob. in PSI4.428.44 , cf. girius, = farina, pollen, Gloss

γύψος.definition: gypsum, Thphr.Lap.64, BGU952.8; cement, Thphr.Lap.65, Ph.Bel.79.5; embedded in cement, D.S.2.10, Arr.An.2.21.4

γωλεός.definition: a hole, Arist.HA603a6 ; Hsch.: heterocl. pl., Nic.Th.125; Lyc.376

γαγγαλίζω.definition: later form of Att. Phryn.77, Anacreont.5.7

γάγγαμον.definition: small round net, esp. for oyster-; umbilical region, Poll.2.169

γάγγραινα.definition: gangrene, Hp.Mochl.33, 2 Ep.Ti.2.17, Dsc.1.61, Plu.2.65d, Gal.18.687

γαγγραίνωσις.definition: becoming gangrenous: gangrenous affection, Hp.Fract.11 , Mochl.30 , Aret.SA2.10

γαζοφυλάκιον.definition: treasury, OGI225.16 , LXX4 Ki.23.11, Str.7.6.1, Ev.Luc.21.1, al

γαζοφύλαξ.definition: treasurer, Phylarch.29, LXX1 Ch.28.1, Str.16.2.40, J.AJ11.1.3, Plu.Demetr.25; written Syria 5.347

Γαιήϊος.definition: sprung from Gaia or Earth; earthly, Nonn.D.37.4; Eranos 13.88

γαιηφάγος.definition: earth-eating, of worms, Numen. ap. Ath.7.305a; cf

γαιονόμος.definition: dwelling in the land: inhabitant, A.Supp.54

γαιοφανής.definition: earth-coloured, in Comp., Archig. ap. Orib.8.2.4 ; the earthy appearance of the moon, Placit.2.30.1 codd

γαλακτιάω.definition: give no milk, Poll.3.50; but Hsch

γαλακτίζω.definition: to be milky in appearance, Dsc.2.144, 175; form a milky way, Phlp.in Mete.117.20

γαλάκτινος.definition: milk-white, AP5.192 ; POxy.267.7 ; milky, PHolm.24.31; v.l. for Dsc.2.175

γαλάκτιον.definition: Dim. of M.Ant.5.4: in pl., fancy bread made with milk, Alciphr.Fr.6.10

γαλακτόομαι.definition: Pass., become milk or milky, Thphr.CP1.7.3, Dsc.3.48; Antyll. ap.Orib.4.11.6, cf. Plu.2.968a

γαλακτοποιΐα.definition: production of milk, Sch. Vat. Nic.Th.944

γαλακτοποτέω.definition: drink milk, Id.Morb.2.51, Int.16, Thphr.HP9.15.4, Str.17.3.8

γαλακτοτροφέω.definition: nourish with milk, LXX4 Ma.13.21, Ph.2.82 , PTeb.399.4

γαλακτουργέω.definition: make of milk, as cheese, Poll.1.251; make milk, as a nursing woman, Sor.2.5

γαλακτουχέω.definition: have or suck milk, Poll.3.50; prob. in Plu.2.64 of

γαλακτοφόρος.definition: giving milk, PLond.1.3.22 , J.BJ3.3.4, Opp.C.1.443; of food, causing an abundant flow of milk, Sch.Nic.Th.553

γαλακτόχρως.definition: milk-coloured, Philyll.4, Nausicr.2: neut. pl., Dsc.3.47: nom. pl. in Opp.C.3.478 is f.l. for

γαλαξιών.definition: name of a Delian month, IG11 .203 A31, al

γαλεοειδής.definition: of the shark kind, Arist.HA565a20:—more usu. ib.505a5, al

γαληνιάζω.definition: = sq., Hp.Vict.2, Ph.1.276, Them.Or.1.17a:—Pass., aor. Simp.in Epict.p.20 D

γαληνιάω.definition: to be calm, find peace, Epicur.Fr.425, cf. Opp.C.1.115, Them.Or.15.195a; Ep.part. AP9.208, 5.34.7

γαληνίζω.definition: calm, still, esp. waves or winds; intr., become calm, prob. in Hp.Morb.Sacr.13; to be calm or tranquil, Alex.178.6, Ph.1.354; Arist.Pr.936a5:—so in Med., Xenocr. ap.Orib.2.58.98

γαληνισμός.definition: calming, Epicur.Ep.1p.32U.; calming of the conscience, Arist.Ep.5

γαλουχέω.definition: suckle, Sor.1.88, J.AJ2.9.5, A.D.Synt.278.1 codd., Sm.1 Ki.6.7

γαμβρεύω.definition: form connexions by marriage, LXXDe.7.3; 2 Es.9.14:—Med., marry, v.l. ib.Ge.38.8:—Pass., to be connected by marriage, J.AJ14.12.1

γαμετή.definition: fem. of sq., married woman, wife, opp. concubine, Hes.Op.406, cf. Pl.Lg.841d, Lys.1.31 , Men.Pk.237, PTeb.104.17 , etc.; Epigr.Gr.310 ; so alone, A.Supp.165 , Arist.Fr.144, POxy.795.4 ; Phld.Ir.p.53 W., cf. Herc. 1457…

γαμέτης.definition: husband, spouse, A.Pr.897 , E.Tr.311 , Euph.107.3; poet. word used by X.Cyr.4.6.3, and late, PLond.5.1711.53 ; Dor. gen. E.Supp.998 :— fem. a wife, dub. in AP5.179 , cf. IPE2.298.10

Γαμηλιών.definition: the seventh month of the Attic year, IG12.6.80, Arist.Mete.343b5, Thphr.HP7.1.2, etc

γαμησείω.definition: Desiderat. of wish to marry, Alciphr.1.13, 3.37

γαμίζω.definition: give a daughter in marriage, A.D.Synt.280.11, 1 Ep.Cor.7.38

γαμίσκω.definition: = Callicrat. ap.Stob.4.28.18:—Med. in Arist.Pol.1335a20; of a woman, PLond.5.1708 :—Pass., Ev.Marc.12.25

γαμοστόλος.definition: preparing a wedding, epith. of Hera; Astrol., name for the seventh house of the horoscope, Paul.Al.M.2

γαμψῶνυξ.definition: with crooked talons, of birds of prey, Il.16.428, Od.22.302; A.Pr.488; of the Sphinx, S.OT1199 ; Nonn.D.12.336, etc.:—also Arist.HA563b20, GA750a11, Plu.2.727c; Plot.6.7.9, pl., Epich.30; of beasts of prey, Arist.HA51…

γαργαίρω.definition: swarm with, Cratin.290, cf. Ar.Fr.359; Sophr.30 : c. dat., Tim.Pers.107

γαργαλίζω.definition: tickle, titillate, Pl.Phlb.47a; metaph., Phld.Mus.p.33K., cf. Ph.2.352; Aristid.Or.34.16, cf. Luc.Cal.21; also of pain, Plu.2.1088a:—Pass., Plot.6.7.34

γαργαλισμός.definition: tickling , Hp.Alim.26, Pl.Smp.189a , Phdr.253e, Epicur.Fr.412 ; Hegesipp.1.16; Ph.1.118, cf. 212 , Plu.2.765c: , and are cited by Erot. s.v. fr. Ar.Fr.175 and Diph.25

γαστρίζω.definition: punch a man in the belly, Ar.Eq.273; stuff, gorge, D.Chr.66.11, cf. Luc.DMeretr.10.4 :—Pass., to be stuffed full, eat gluttonously, Theopomp. Hist.187, Men.Pk.98, Posidon.18, Luc.Rh. Pr.24, Alciphr.3.45; Ath.3.96f

γαστριμαργία.definition: gluttony, Hp.Int.6, Pl.Phd.81e , Eus.Mynd.9, Andronic.Rhod.p.572 M.; pl., Luc.Am.42

γαστρίμαργος.definition: gluttonous , Pi.O.1.52, Arist.EN1118b19, Xanth.12, Cerc.16.2, Nic.Dam.p.22 D., etc.: Sup. Ph.2.22

γαστρολογία.definition: the Greek Almanach des Gourmands, written by Archestratus, Ath.3.104b, 7.278b; also cited by the title of Id.1.4e, 2.56c

γαστρόπτης.definition: vessel for cooking sausages, Demioprat.ap. Poll.10.105:—fem. IG11.161B128 , but ib.199 B 79

γαστρορραφία.definition: sewing up of a belly-wound, Scrib. Larg.206, Gal.10.416, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.23.46

γαστροφορέω.definition: bear in the belly of a bottle, AP9.232

γαστροχάρυβδις.definition: with a gulf of a belly, Cratin.397

γαστρόχειρ.definition: living by one's hands, written in Str.8.6.11, EM221; cf

γαυρίαμα.definition: arrogance, exultation, LXXJu.10.8, Phld.Mort.18, Plu.Aem.27, etc

γαυριάω.definition: mostly pres. Aet. and Med., aor. 1 LXXJu.9.7:—bear oneself proudly, prance, prop. of horses, Plu.Lyc.22:—Med., X.Eq.10.16; to be splendid, . . Cratin.301; to be luxuriant, Jul.Or.4.155c; of persons, Phld.Vit.p.27 J., …

γαῦρος.definition: exulting in, Archil.58; E.Supp.862: abs., haughty, disdainful, Id.Fr.788, Ar.Ra.282; Luc.Nigr.5, cf. Jul.Caes.319d; in good sense, splendid, D.Chr.67.5 , D.C.68.31; epith. of IG7.544,545 ; also, skittish, Theoc.11.21:…

γαυρότης.definition: exultation, Plu.Marc.6; of a horse or ass, Id.Pel.22, Mar.38

γαυρόω.definition: make proud, only aor. Plu.Cor.15, D.C.55.6 is to be read in E.Fr.52.8): elsewh. Pass. = exult, Batr.262a; Ph.2.125: c. dat., pride oneself on, Ps.-Phoc.53; PFlor.367.11 ; E.Or.1532, cf. Ba.1144; X.Hier.2.15: impf. Bab…

γαυσόομαι.definition: to be bent, pf. Pass. Sor.Fract.19:—Act., Hsch

γεγωνίσκω.definition: lengthd. pres. for cry aloud; c. acc. rei, tell out, proclaim, A.Pr.627, E.El.809

γεῖσον.definition: coping of a wall, E.Or.1570, 1620, Ph.1158, 1180; metaph., hem or border of a garment, Ar.Fr.762; Poll.2.49

γεῖσος.definition: - foreg., LXXEz.43.17: pl., BCH35.76 ; dat. pl. OGI483.127 :—also Gloss

γειτνία.definition: = I, Hp.Ep.23, OGI383.98 : in pl., adjoining areas, PTeb.14.10 , PAvrom.2 A8 , PAmh.2.68.4 , etc

γειτνίασις.definition: = neighbourhood; a neighbourhood, district, OGI483.28, 32 , Ph.2.475 , Plu.Cor.24; Id.Per.19

γειτνιάω.definition: pres. (3sg. impf. S.Ichn.232, and; border on, resemble, Arist.Pol.1295a33; Id.Rh.1367b12; Ph.2.548; Metrod.Herc.831.3: later fut. Gal.3.690: aor. Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.1

γειτονεύω.definition: = sq., c. dat., X.Vect.1.8, Str.3.3.8, al.: abs., Id.4.6.8, al., Phld.Ir.p.48 W., etc.:—Med., Hp.Fract.18

γειτονέω.definition: = c. dat., A.Pers.311, Supp.780 , v.l. in S.OC1525, SIG 685.38 , Procop.Aed.4.1; Call.Iamb.1.300: metaph., Plot.3.9.2, cf. 1.2.5

γειτόνημα.definition: neighbourhood, neighbouring place, Alcm.116; Pl.Lg.705a, cf. Ael.Ep.13, Procop.Aed.1.11, al., Agath.3.6; Aret.CA2.3, cf. CD2.6; proximity, Plot.5.1.3

γειτονία.definition: quarter, ward, in a city, J.BJ7.4.1:— hence chief official of a ward, Hsch. s.v

γελασείω.definition: Desiderat. of to be ready to laugh, Pl.Phd.64b

γελάσιμος.definition: laughable, Stratt.72, Luc.Somn.5: less correct than Phryn.206

γελασῖνος.definition: laugher, of Democritus, Ael.VH4.20; the grinners, i. e. the front teeth, which show when one laughs, Poll.2.91

γελγιδόομαι.definition: Pass., form a compound bulb, of garlic, Thphr.HP7.4.11

γελοιάζω.definition: only pres., jest, LXXGe.19.14, Aristarch. ap. Ath.2.39e, Plu.2.231c, Arr.Epict.3.16.4, Jul.Caes.306b, Procop.Arc.9

γελοιαστής.definition: jester, buffoon, Ptol. Megalop.2, LXXJb.31.5, Poll.5.128, prob. in Luc.Merc.Cond.4

γελοιάω.definition: Ep. for in aor. part. h.Ven.49

γελωτοποιέω.definition: to create, make laughter, esp.by buffoonery, X.Smp.3.11, Pl.R.606c, Hyp.Phil.2

γέμω.definition: used only in pres. and impf., to be full, prop; c. gen. rei, to be full of, Th.7.25; Pl.Criti.117e; X.An.4.6.27; of animals, to be laden. Posidon.5: metaph., A.Ag.613, cf. S.OT4; E.HF1245; Pl.Lg.649d; Id.Grg.525a; Phl…

γενεαλογέω.definition: Ion. trace a pedigree, Hdt.2.146; draw out one's pedigree, ib.143; X.Smp.4.51; Plu.2.894b; . . , Id.Lyc.1, Paus.5.14.9; Luc.Salt.7: abs., Isoc.15.180, Thphr.Char.28.2:—Pass., Hp.Septim.4; Hdt.6.54; Pl.Ti.23b; Ep.Hebr.…

γενεαλογία.definition: tracing a pedigree, Pl.Cra.396c, al.: in pl., Isoc.11.8; title of work by Hecataeus; Plb.9.2.1, cf. 1 Ep.Ti.1.4, Jul.Or.7.205c

γενεάρχης.definition: = IG3.1278, cf. OGI531 ; = , Apollod.2.1.4, Heraclit.All.22, Jul.Ep.89, etc.; chief, sheikh, CR Acad.Inscr. 1924.28

γενεθλιαλογέω.definition: cast nativities, practise astrology, Str.16.1.6:— Med., Cat.Cod.Astr.1.170

γενεθλιαλογία.definition: casting of nativities, astrology, J.AJ18.6.9, Ptol.Tetr.7, Iamb.Myst.9.1, Hierocl.Prov. ap.Phot.p.172 B

γενεθλιαλόγος.definition: caster of nativities, Ptol.Tetr.13, Hierocl.Prov. ap.Phot.p.172B., Iamb.Myst.1.18

γενειάζω.definition: Dor. get a beard, come to man's estate, D.H.1.76, AP12.12 ; Theoc.11.9, cf. CIG 3715 : pf. Philem.15

γενείασις.definition: growth of the beard, in pl., Plot.4.3.13

γενειάσκω.definition: begin to get a beard, Pl.Smp.181d, X.Cyr.4.6.5; IG3.1314

γενειάτης.definition: Ep. and Ion. bearded, Theoc.17.33, Luc.Bis Acc.28, Jul.Or.4.131a, Call.Dian.90:—fem. Sophr.31; Ion. Eratosth.12

γένειον.definition: part covered by the beard, chin; beard, Hdt.6.117: pl., Theoc.6.36, J.AJ11.5.3, Paus.2.10.3, Theo Sm.p.104H

γενεσιάρχης.definition: creator, LXXWi.13.3; of the Sun, Jul.Astr.in Cat.Cod.Astr.1.136.2

γενέσιος.definition: = Plu.2.402a; epith. of; shrine of Posidon Paus.l.c

γενεσιουργέω.definition: bring into being, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44

γενετή.definition: = II.3, from the hour of birth, Il.24.535, Od.18.6; Arist.EN1144b6; opp. ib.1154a33; later Iamb.VP30.171

γενετήρ.definition: = Epic.Alex.Adesp.3.10, Arist.Mu.397a4, IG3.716, Coluth.373, Tryph.294: in pl., parents, IG7.2543, Nonn.D.4.61, al

γενέτης.definition: begetter, ancestor, E.Or.1011; produced, Olymp.in Mete.94.9

γενηματογραφέω.definition: sequester produce of land for non- payment of taxes, in Pass., PFay.23.14, 26.8,al., BGU291,599

γενηματοφύλαξ.definition: custodian of crops, PMagd.1.10 , etc.:—hence PTeb.ined., and PTeb.27.4 , al. , PRyl.90.50

γεννάδας.definition: noble, generous, Ar.Ra.179; Pl.Phdr.243c, cf. Arist.EN1100b32; highly bred, Polem.Phgn.78; notable, c. inf., Luc.Hist.Conscr.33

γενναιάζω.definition: to be brave, Sch.E.Hipp.206:—also Suid. s.v

γενναιοπρεπής.definition: befitting a noble: only in Adv. Ar.Pax988

γενναῖος.definition: also E.Hec.592: :—true; of persons, high-born, noble, Archil.107, etc.; Hdt.1.173; S.OT1469; Id.Fr.107.3; Pl.Tht.174e; opp. Arist.Pol.1296b22; so of animals, well- bred, Pl.R.375a, X.Cyr.1.4.15; opp. Arist.HA558b16

γενναιότης.definition: the character of a nobility, E.Ph.1680, Th.3.82; of land, fertility, X.Cyr.8.3.38, Plb.3.44.8; noble birth, J.AJ19.3.1; high spirit, of colts, Max.Tyr.7.8

γεννήτωρ.definition: Dor. = A.Supp.206, E.Hipp.683, Jul.Or.2.51d, v.l. in Arist.Mu.397b21; Pl.Lg.878a: pl., ib.869a; IG3.636: metaph. of numbers, Iamb.in Nic.p.56 P., al

γεράνειον.definition: a kind of truffle, Eust.1017.19; = Thphr.HP1.6.9, ap.Ath.2.62a ; but dist. from ib.1.6.5, ap.Ath.2.61f

γερονταγωγέω.definition: guide an old man, S.OC348: c.acc., Id.Fr.487, parodied by Com.Adesp.11, cf. Ar.Eq.1099

γερόντειος.definition: belonging to an old man or old age, Ar.Fr.715

γεροντεύω.definition: to be a senator, IG5.254 , al.:—Med., Hsch.s.v

γεροντοκομεῖον.definition: hospital for the old, Cod.Just.1.3.45.1:—also Subst. warden of such a hospital, Just.Nov.7.1

γεροντομανία.definition: craze or dotage of old men, name of a play by Anaxandrides, Arist.Rh.1413b26

γερούσιος.definition: for or befitting the wine drunk only by the chiefs, Il.4.259, Od.13.8; an oath taken by them, Il.22.119; perquisite of chiefs, Hsch

γερροφύλαξ.definition: defender of wicker-work barrier, Sammelb.1918, prob.in OGI111

γερροχελώνη.definition: penthouse, mantlet, used in siege- works, Ph.Bel.98.19

γεῦσις.definition: sense of taste, Democr.11; a tasting, LXXDa.5.2

γευστήριον.definition: cup for tasting with, Ar.Fr.299, Pherecr.143.3

γεφυρίζω.definition: abuse from the causeway, in the procession from Athens to Eleusis, Hsch., Suid.: hence, abuse freely, Plu.Sull.6,13

γεφύρωσις.definition: furnishing with a causeway or bridge, Str.1.3.18 ; Arr.An.5.7.3; in concrete sense, Ctes.Fr.29.17

γεωγραφέω.definition: describe the earth's surface, Str.1.1.16, Arist.Mu.393b20:—Pass., geographic description, title of Strabo's work, Ath.14.657f

γεωγραφία.definition: geography, Phld.Po.5.1425.2, Str. l. c; geographical work, Democr.14c, Plu.Thes.1 , Porph.Antr.4

γεωγράφος.definition: earth-describing: Subst., geographer, Str.1.1.16, al.; i. e. Strabo, Eust. ad D.P.11, al

γεωδαισία.definition: land-dividing: mensuration, opp. the science of geometry, Arist.Metaph.997b26, Jul.Gal.178b, Procl.in Euc.p.25 F

γεώλοφος.definition: crested with earth, Str.16.2.16; Subst. hill, hillock, X.Cyr.3.3.28 codd., Plb.1.75.4, Ph.1.191; Theoc.1.13, Numen. ap. Ath.7.305a

γεωμαντεία.definition: geomancy, Varr. ap. Isid.8.9.13: Subst. Id. ap. Serv.Virg.A.3.359

γεωμετρέω.definition: prop., measure, survey land, BGU12.27 (ii; generally, measure, c. acc., Ar.Av.995; Pl.Tht.173e, cf. X.Smp.6.8, BGU12.27 , Luc.Icar.21

γεωμέτρης.definition: land-measurer, ib.28 :—but usu., geometer, Pl.Tht.143b, al., cf. Men.495, CIG3544

γεωμέτρητος.definition: geometrical, Procl.in Euc.p.201 F.; ib.p.185 F

γεωμετρία.definition: Ion. geometry, Hdt.2.109; land-survey, PTeb.24.42 , cf. POxy.499.27

γεωμορία.definition: portion of land, Nic.Al.10: pl., farms; = Alciphr.1.4, AP7.532

γεωνόμος.definition: one who distributes land, IG12.45; receiving a portion of distributed lands, colonist, D.C.38.1:—also Phryn.PSp.57 B

γεωπονέω.definition: till the ground, Ph.1.212; E.Rh.75; Heph.Astr.2.28

γεωπονία.definition: Ion. tillage, Orph.Fr.280, Epigr.Gr.446 , Max.Tyr.27.5:—also Ps.-Phoc.161, Them.Or.30.350a, Hld.10.6

γεωπόνος.definition: husbandman, AP7.175 , 281 ; labourer, opp. Ph.1.211:—also Damocr. ap.Gal.13.40, Agath.2.17 , Babr.108.14: E.Supp.420: Them.Or.30.350c, Hld.5.23

γεωργέω.definition: to be a husbandman, farmer, Pl.Lg.805e; c. acc., till, plough, cultivate, Ar.Ec.592; Th.3.88; D.18.41:—Pass., of land, IG9.61 ; SIG685.80 ; Arist.Pr.896a10

γεώργημα.definition: in pl., operations of husbandry, Pl.Lg.674c

γεωργήσιμος.definition: tilled or fit for tillage, Arist.Pr.924a22, Str.16.4.18, Plb.1.56.4

γεωργία.definition: tillage, Th.1.11, etc; in pl., farms, tilled land, Isoc.7.32, cf. Pl.Lg.806d, Luc.Prom.14, etc.; rarely in sg., D.30.30

γεωρύχος.definition: burrowing, Str.3.2.6, cf. Hsch. s.v. mole, prob. cj. in Gloss

γεωφανής.definition: looking like earth, Archig. ap.Orib.8.2.4: esp. in pl., a spot where a kind of ochre was dug, at Samos, Thphr.Lap.61:—so or title of speech by Din., D.H.Din.10, cf. Sch.Nic.Al.149, Poll.7.99, EM229.21

γηγενής.definition: Dor. Hdn.Gr.2.419:—earthborn; earthborn, of primeval men, Hdt.8.55; A.Supp.250; Pl.Plt.269b, cf. Arist.GA762b29; of the Thebans, Trag.Adesp.84; LXXWi.7.1; of body, opp. soul, Pl.Lg.727e

γηθόσυνος.definition: also Orph.H.27.14, AP6.235 :—joyful, glad, Il.7.122; 13.82. Adv. Hp.Ep.17, Suid

γύμνητις.definition: fem. of in signf. of II.3, Plu.2.332b

γυμνοπαιδική.definition: dance of naked boys, Ath.14.630d: pl., PhldMus.p.15K

γυμνοπερίβολος.definition: bare of coverings, epith. of Ps.-Callisth.3.5

γυμνοπόδιον.definition: kind of sandal or slipper, Poll.7.94

γυμνορρύπαρος.definition: naked and dirty, of Zeno, D.L.7.16

γυμνοσπέρματος.definition: and having the seed with no apparent pericarp, Thphr.HP1.11.2 and 3

γύμνωσις.definition: stripping, Plu.Lyc.14, cf; exposure, LXXGe.9.22; his defenceless side , Th.5.71

γυμνωτέος.definition: one must strip, Gal.10.448: pl., Them.Or.23.294c

γυναικάνηρ.definition: woman-man: dat. pl., Epich.218, cf. Eust.1132.32

γυναικάριον.definition: Dim. of Diocl.Com.11, Epict.Ench.7, 2 Ep.Ti.3.6, M.Ant.5.11

γυναικεῖος.definition: in bad sense, womanish, effeminate, Archil.9.10; Ar.Th.151; Pl.Alc.1.127a; Id.R.469d. Adv. Id.Lg.731d; Eus.Mynd.54; D.C.38.18

γυναικεραστέω.definition: to be a lover of women, and woman-lover, Poll.3.68,70

γυναικίζω.definition: to be womanish, play the woman, Hp.Aër.22; muliebria pati, Luc.Gall.19: = Hsch

γυναικισμός.definition: womanish weakness, Plb.30.18.5, cf. Phld.Mus.p.16K., D.S.31.15, Plu.Caes.63

γυναικοδίδακτος.definition: taught by a woman, Olymp.in Alc.p.136C

γυναικοθοίνας.definition: feasted by the women or feaster of women, epith. of Ares at Tegea, Paus.8.48.4

γυναικόθυμος.definition: of womanish mind, Ptol.Tetr.162. Adv. Plb.2.8.12; of a man, Id.32.15.9

γυναικοκρατέομαι.definition: Pass., to be ruled by women, Arist.Pol.1269b24, D.S.2.45, Plu.2.755c

γυναικοκρατία.definition: dominion of women, Arist.Pol.1313b33, Plu.Cat. Ma.8: title of plays by Amphis and Alexis

γυναικομανέω.definition: to be mad for women, Ar.Th.576, J.BJ1.22.3

γυναικομανής.definition: mad for women, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.167, Ph.2.312, Gal.5.396, AP12.86 , Luc.Alex.11

γυναικόμασθος.definition: or having breasts like a woman: abnormal development of the mamma, Gal.19.444, cf. Paul.Aeg.6.46

γυναικόμιμος.definition: aping women, A.Pr.1005; S.Fr.769; E.Antiop.iiA7 A. ; Id.Ba.980

γυναικονόμος.definition: supervisor of women, title of magistrate at Athens and elsewhere, Timocl.32.3, Men.272, Arist.Pol.1299a22, Philoch.103, IG5.170 , 1390.26 , SIG1219.17

γυναικοπρεπής.definition: befitting women, womanish, Plu.2.102e: Comp., Procl.Par.Ptol.203

γυναικότροφος.definition: reared by a woman, Suid. s.v

γυναικοφίλης.definition: Dor. woman-loving, Polyzel.10, Theoc.8.[60]: voc. AP6.78

γυναικωνῖτις.definition: women's apartments in a house; as Adj., the court of the women's apartments, D.S.17.50; Ph.1.312

γυναιμανής.definition: = mad for women; making women mad, Hsch

γυπάριον.definition: Dim. of sq., nest, cranny, Ar.Eq.793

γυρίτης.definition: bread of the finest meal, Gp.20.41, Hsch

γυροδρόμος.definition: running round in a circle, a millstone, AP9.20

γυροειδής.definition: like a circle, round. Adv. Dsc.2.173

γυρόω.definition: make round, LXXSi.43.12; bend; plant in a Arat.9, Ph.2.294; make a round a tree, ib.402, Gp.4.3.1:—Med., dig, trench, Nic.Al.514

γύψινος.definition: made of gypsum, EM530.15; room plastered with gypsum, BGU 1028.88

γωνιάζω.definition: place at an angle, Porph.in Cat.132.31

γωνιαῖος.definition: on or at the angle, LXXJb.38.6; angular, i. e. hard to pronounce, Pl.Com.67

γωνιασμός.definition: squaring off corners, Lys.Fr.61; name of a proposition in geometry, Hsch.: metaph., finishing of verses by square and rule, Ar.Ra.956

γωνιοβόμβυξ.definition: one that buzzes in a corner, nickname of Grammarians, Herodic. ap. Ath.5.222a

γωνιόομαι.definition: Pass., become angular, Dsc.3.7; Procl.in Euc.p.163F

γωνιοποιέομαι.definition: form into an angle:—Pass., Erot. s.v

γαμητικῶς.definition: Adv. with an inclination for marriage, Hsch. s.v

γεγηθότως.definition: Adv. pf. of with joy, Hld.7.5, Ph.2.295

γενεῆθεν.definition: Adv. from birth, by descent, Arat.260; AP7.415

γῆθεν.definition: Adv. out of or from the earth, A.Th.247, Eu.904, S.OC1591; from beneath, Id.El.453: in late Prose, J.AJ4.3.2; Luc.Icar.4

γονικόθεν.definition: Adv. by inheritance from parents, PMasp.151.182
